description.en-US: The human-facing identifier of this settlement unit. Immutable: it is printed, quoted on the phone and referenced by payment records, so changing one would orphan every mention of it.

The sale this bill settles. BR 35's field list omits it, which cannot be right: a bill that names no order cannot have its allocations checked against one, and BR 36's invariant is stated over the bills OF an order. Immutable, because moving a bill between orders would break that invariant on both.

Whether this bill is still being settled. 'settled' means the money is in and the allocations are frozen; 'cancelled' means it was superseded by a split or a merge, and it is kept rather than deleted (BR 83) because the lineage rows point at it.

How much of this bill has been paid, on the same scale the order uses (D-18). Note 'overpaid' is present although D-18's list omits it: BR 42 permits taking more than the bill is for when the cash-change policy allows, so a bill genuinely can reach that state, and a bill unable to express it would have to be recorded as merely 'paid' - losing the fact that change is owed.

The currency this bill settles in, copied from its order. Immutable, and a merge refuses to combine bills that disagree on it (BR 74) rather than converting - Sales has no FX and inventing a rate would be a pricing decision nobody authorised.
The sum of this bill's line allocations before discount and tax.
This bill's share of the order's discounts. Positive by convention, like the order's own total: it answers how much was given away, not what a step did to a number.

This bill's share of the order's tax, allocated rather than recomputed. Recomputing tax per bill would let the bills of one order sum to a different tax than the order was charged, which is the reconciliation failure BR 36's invariant exists to prevent.

What this bill is for, and what a payment is measured against. The sum of these across every bill of an order equals the order's own total EXACTLY (BR 36) - not approximately, which is why the allocator assigns the rounding residual rather than letting it vanish.
When the money was fully in. Null while the bill is still open; set once and never cleared, because a settled bill that reopens is a new commercial event rather than an undo.
When this bill was superseded by a split or a merge. The bill itself stays (BR 83); this records when it stopped being the live settlement unit.
